knowledge_point.title: Finding the Points Where a Gradient Vanishes

question.:question/problem: Given $f(x,y)=3 \left(y + 3\right)^{2} + \ln{\left(\left(x - 1\right)^{2} + 2 \right)}$, find the points $(x,y)$ where $\nabla f=\mathbf 0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
A gradient vanishes exactly when every component vanishes. Differentiate with respect to each variable, holding the others constant.

$$
\begin{aligned}f_{x}&=\frac{2 \left(x - 1\right)}{\left(x - 1\right)^{2} + 2} \\ f_{y}&=6 y + 18\end{aligned}
$$

Set all components equal to zero:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2 \left(x - 1\right)}{\left(x - 1\right)^{2} + 2}&=0 \\ 6 y + 18&=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

To write the simultaneous equations compactly, let $u=x - 1,\ v=y + 3$. Since $u^2+2>0$, the first component vanishes exactly when $u=0$. The other equation gives $v=0$. Recover the original coordinates using $x=u + 1,\ y=v - 3$.

Therefore, the complete set of points in the domain is $(1,-3)$. Each satisfies every component equation.

knowledge_point.title: Finding the Points Where a Gradient Vanishes

question.:question/problem: Given $f(x,y)=- x^{2} + 2 x \left(y - 1\right) + \left(y - 1\right)^{2}$, find the points $(x,y)$ where $\nabla f=\mathbf 0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
A gradient vanishes exactly when every component vanishes. Differentiate with respect to each variable, holding the others constant.

$$
\begin{aligned}f_{x}&=- 2 x + 2 y - 2 \\ f_{y}&=2 x + 2 y - 2\end{aligned}
$$

Set all components equal to zero:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}- 2 x + 2 y - 2&=0 \\ 2 x + 2 y - 2&=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

To write the simultaneous equations compactly, let $u=x,\ v=y - 1$. The first equation gives $u=v$. Substitute into the second:

$$
\begin{aligned}4 v&=0 \\ v&=0 \\ u&=0\end{aligned}
$$

 Recover the original coordinates using $x=u,\ y=v + 1$.

Therefore, the complete set of points in the domain is $(0,1)$. Each satisfies every component equation.

knowledge_point.title: Finding the Points Where a Gradient Vanishes

question.:question/problem: Given $f(x,y)=\left(x^{2} - \left(y + 2\right)^{2}\right) e^{- 2 x}$, find the points $(x,y)$ where $\nabla f=\mathbf 0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
A gradient vanishes exactly when every component vanishes. Differentiate with respect to each variable, holding the others constant.

$$
\begin{aligned}f_{x}&=\left(- 2 x^{2} + 2 x + 2 \left(y + 2\right)^{2}\right) e^{- 2 x} \\ f_{y}&=- 2 \left(y + 2\right) e^{- 2 x}\end{aligned}
$$

Set all components equal to zero:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}\left(- 2 x^{2} + 2 x + 2 \left(y + 2\right)^{2}\right) e^{- 2 x}&=0 \\ - 2 \left(y + 2\right) e^{- 2 x}&=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

To write the simultaneous equations compactly, let $u=x,\ v=y + 2$. Since $e^{- 2 u}>0$, divide both equations by this factor. The second equation gives $v=0$. Substitution into the first gives

$$
\begin{aligned}u \left(2 - 2 u\right)&=0 \\ u&=0\quad\text{or}\quad u=1\end{aligned}
$$

Keep both factors; dividing by $u$ would lose a point. Recover the original coordinates using $x=u,\ y=v - 2$.

Therefore, the complete set of points in the domain is $(0,-2)$ and $(1,-2)$. Each satisfies every component equation.
